newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Thyssen says Krupp to bear costs of merger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Thyssen says Krupp to bear costs of merger.

text.p: Germany's Thyssen AG on Thursday hailed its steel merger with rival Krupp as the "best possible solution", saying it would not pay any restructuring costs and would have its profits guaranteed by Krupp from the start.
Chairman Dieter Vogel, speaking after Thyssen's supervisory board gave unanimous approval to the deal, said the hostile takeover that Krupp abandoned would have collapsed under a mountain of debt.
"We are convinced that this solution offers advantages over all others discussed in recent days," Vogel told a news conference at his company's Duesseldorf headquarters.
"It makes it possible not to impose compulsory redundancies and offers the best possible basis for securing production facilities in the long term."
Vogel also said the number of job losses resulting from the merger would be lower than announced by the two sides when they signed a memorandum of understanding on Wednesday.
From a workforce of 23,600 at the start of 1997, 6,600 jobs would be shed by the year 2001, he said. The companies said previously that around 8,000 workers would have to go.
Thousands of workers at three Krupp steel mills were not convinced and continued their week-long stoppage to try to secure written confirmation that none of them would be fired.

Vogel said the Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp group would bear all the restructuring costs from merging the two groups' quality steel operations to create a business with sales of 11 billion marks ($6.5 billion) and output of 15 million tonnes a year.
